sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: L2: construct used in HEK293 nAChR interaction assay (functional result not stated in clip). L1: expression confirmed by western blot in HEK293 cell lysates. Neither clip reports a quantitative functional outcome.
sites.rationale: LYNX1 is a GPI-anchored Ly-6/uPAR family protein with signal peptide residues 1–20 and a fully extracellular mature domain (residues 21–116); there is no TM segment, so the only conventional extracellular terminus for tag insertion is the mature N-terminus immediately after signal-peptide cleavage. Both L1 (mCherry-Lynx1) and L2 (FLAG-Lynx1) describe N-terminal fusions to the full-length protein used in HEK293 cells, consistent with tag placement after residue 20 (the last signal-peptide residue, A) and before residue 21 (L, the first mature residue). No residue is named in either clip, so the junction is topology-derived from the single available extracellular terminus. L2 is used as the primary clip because it explicitly describes a short epitope tag (FLAG) in a functional experimental context. Human LYNX1 with an N-terminal FLAG tag was cloned into pCherry/P2A vector and transfected into HEK293 cells to examine nAChR interactions (L2). Separately, an mCherry-Lynx1 N-terminal fusion was co-expressed with nAChR subunits in HEK293 cells and confirmed by western blot (L1). Neither paper names a specific residue; LYNX1 has a signal peptide (residues 1–20) and is GPI-anchored with no TM domain, leaving the mature N-terminus (after residue 20) as the sole extracellular terminus accessible for tagging.

sources.claim: The DNA fragments encoding human Lynx1 [ NM_177457 ] and mouse Ly6H [ NM_011837 ] with N-terminal FLAG-tag were synthesised by GeneArt Gene Synthesis and inserted into XhoI- and BamHI-digested pCherry/P2A vector, in frame, at the back of Cherry/P2A using In-Fusion HD Cloning Kit.

literature_notes: LYNX1 is a GPI-anchored protein (Ly-6/neurotoxin family) with signal peptide residues 1–20 and a single extracellular domain spanning residues 21–116; there is no transmembrane segment and no intracellular domain. The C-terminus (residue 116) carries the GPI anchor signal and is processed co-translationally; it is not accessible for conventional tag insertion. Both ledger lines (L1, L2) describe N-terminal tags on the full-length protein in HEK293 cells, both pointing to the same junction (insert_after_residue=20). Because they pin the same position, one site is reported (using L2 as primary, L1 noted in rationale). No internal loop insertions are supported by the ledger. No residue-level position is named in either clip, so position_evidence is topology_derived. Validation is detected_only because neither clip reports a quantitative functional result for the tagged construct.
